If you only remember one thing: A I just became a real election issue, and tech is feeling it in the markets.

Number one. The midterms were a referendum on A I.
From your Politico Decoded. Its piece, How Big Tech Lost the Midterms, says an industry push against A I regulation sparked a counterforce. A I safety advocates, consumer groups, and Democratic strategists raised millions for candidates who want stronger oversight. Data centers, kids' safety, and corporate power all reached voters. The coalition is already split on what to prioritize. Why it matters: expect A I and data center rules to be a twenty twenty seven agenda item.

Number two. Markets and data centers wobble.
From your The Information weekend edition. The Nasdaq fell five and a half percent on Thursday, and recovered some on Friday. A Dutch bank is trying to sell about half a billion dollars of data center loans, some tied to Open A I's Stargate. Anthropic investors are reportedly nervous about its I P O valuation target. Google is spending fifteen billion dollars in Malaysia, and announced a seventeen billion dollar site in Wyoming. New York and Amsterdam tightened data center rules. Why it matters: the build out is moving overseas, and the financing is being questioned.

Number three. A I model and product news.
From The Neuron. The research group Metr estimates Anthropic's capability progress is running about twice its earlier pace. Most of the report was redacted. Open A I released G P T six Cyber to vetted security researchers, and rated its cyber capabilities Critical. The Justice Department launched a Super Intelligence Task Force on A I enabled crime and foreign threats. Perplexity launched always on Teammates agents. And Claude added a read only personal finance beta. Why it matters: the frontier is accelerating, and governments are starting to police it.

Number four. Chips and China.
Per the Financial Times, Nvidia told cloud customers to keep Chinese clients under forty nine percent of their base. It was a verbal instruction, and Nvidia hasn't confirmed it. The Information also reports on smuggling of memory chips to China from South Korea. Why it matters: export controls are now being enforced through company policy, not just law.

Number five. Good news.
Few fresh stories today. One to watch: humanitarian groups keep pushing A I into aid work, including the Anthropic and Gates Foundation two hundred million dollar commitment reported earlier this year.

Also in your Reads. The New Yorker on the politics of Stephen Miller and Trump after the election, and Cutlefish on the loss of positive friction.

The thread: A I's politics caught up with its money this week. That's your briefing. Have a good Sunday.
